name: CatMousePursuit-v1
summary: Symmetric grid pursuit-evasion. A cat must catch a mouse; the mouse must reach its nest. Both are learned policies. Reference JS implementation: env.js (port 1:1 to Python — same seed must yield the same map).

pillars.note: single cells, never adjacent to more than one wall — keeps corridors open

generation.connectivity: >=94% of free cells in one region, else reseed
generation.nests: CONFIGURABLE, default 2, max 3. Each is a free cell within 4 cells of a short edge with TWO INDEPENDENT APPROACHES — walling any single neighbour must leave it reachable. Holes are kept >= 10 apart (BFS) so one cat cannot cover two. One hole makes camping it a dominant strategy: measured, 27% of low-skill episodes then die on the step limit, against 8% with two.
generation.nestField: multi-source BFS — distance to the NEAREST hole
generation.mouseSpawn: BFS distance to the nearest hole >= 72% of this map's maximum. A fixed range cannot work across hole counts: two holes on opposite walls halve the longest possible trek.
generation.catSpawn: BFS distance to mouse >= 10, and to the nearest hole in [4, 85% of max] (camping an exit must be viable)

traps.placement: 3 sit ON the mouse's BFS shortest route to the nest (spaced, skipping the first 3 cells so nobody spawns trapped), 2 flank that route so detouring is not automatically safe, the rest scattered; nest mouth kept clear; a map that cannot place 4 is reseeded
traps.why: a trap parked off the walked route is never learned and never seen

symmetry: Full. Identical speed (1 cell/step), identical action space, identical vision cone, identical trap effect. Only the sensor suite and the objective differ.

actionSpace.note: A movement action also sets `facing`, which aims the vision cone. `stay` preserves facing. Blocked moves are no-ops but still turn the agent.

vision.occlusion: walls block rays and line of sight

hearing.trigger: only when the cat actually moved this step (frozen cat is silent)
hearing.noiseSigma: 0.10 + 0.055 * distance, applied to the reported cat position
hearing.output: [x/W, y/H, confidence] or null; confidence = 1 - d/range

scent.note: the mouse deposits scent 1.0 on its cell each step; the whole field decays *0.93 per step. The cat reads the strongest cell within BFS range 6.

shared.nestBearing: radians, both agents know where the nest is

dynamics.resolution: simultaneous — both actions applied in the same step

traps.effect: stepping on a trap freezes that agent for 5 steps; the trap stays armed
traps.note: traps hit cat and mouse identically — the asymmetry is entirely in what each has learned to avoid

termination.catch: capture radius 1 — same cell, Manhattan distance 1, or the two swapped through each other -> cat wins. A same-cell-only rule is nearly unsatisfiable with simultaneous moves at equal speed: the pair just trade places forever.
termination.escape: mouse reaches ANY hole -> mouse wins. CHECKED BEFORE catch: reaching the hole beats a simultaneous catch, otherwise sitting on the hole is an absolute strategy.
termination.timeout: step == maxSteps -> draw (counts for neither side)

reward.note: Shaping terms are a starting point, not a requirement. Terminal terms are the contract.

training.pairing: self-play within an algorithm: each algorithm trains its own cat AND its own mouse against each other (3 algorithms x 2 roles = 6 policies).
training.fairness: All three arenas run the identical map and identical spawns for a given round seed.
training.finals: Take argmax catch-rate cat and argmax escape-rate mouse across algorithms, run a 5-round series on a fresh map.
training.measuredBalance: Reference run, 432 episodes over the 6 shipped maps: 39% catch, 53% escape, 8% draw; 338 trap hits, 14 of them after episode 28. Use these as a sanity target — a cat under 20% or draws over 20% means something is wrong with the rules, not the learner.

metrics.curves: rolling window of 160 episodes, one point per episode

frameProtocol.purpose: What the visualiser consumes. Implement this and the UI needs no other change.

methods.init(cfg): cfg = { grid:{w,h}, arenas:[{algo, seed}] }. Called once.
methods.nextFrame(): Called once per animation frame. Return null to hold the previous frame.

arenas.map: OPTIONAL, only when it changed: { grid:number[], nest:[x,y], traps:[[x,y]], blocks:[{x,y,w,h}], pillars:[[x,y]] }

cat.x: float (may be fractional for smooth interpolation)
cat.mode: string, drives the on-screen thought line

registry.note: Adding a fourth algorithm = one entry in agents.js ALGOS plus one emblem branch in AlgoEmblem.dc.html. Nothing else in the UI is algorithm-aware.

roleColorConvention.algorithmIdentity: emblem + accent object (cat collar and inner ears, mouse scarf)
roleColorConvention.roleIdentity: species and cone colour, never fur — cat is slate (#7e90ad) and large, mouse is tan (#d09b6a) and small; cat cones warm (#ff7a54), mouse cones cool (#6ee2ff)

neutral.trap: #f2b544 pressure plate in a steel jaw trap; armed = open toothed ring, triggered = closed vertical lens with sparks, rendered from the victim frozen counter

roleColorConvention.stateReads: alert = wide eyes + exclamation tick + brighter cone; frozen = X eyes + dashed frost ring; facing = pupil offset and horizontal flip, characters never rotate
